page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor, executing on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Cache sizing consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on external network-attached Premium Storage disks for persistence.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate balanced single-threaded capabilities offset by moderate multi-core throughput typical of a 4-vCPU envelope. The EPYC architecture delivers strong single-core results in stress-ng at 2701.97, alongside mid-range Geekbench single-core performance of 1490.0 and encryption scores of 4304.48 supported by hardware AES and SHA instructions. Conversely, parallel throughput is bounded by the four-thread ceiling, resulting in lower-tier Geekbench multi-core scores (3369.0), PassMark CPU scores (6162.2), and multi-threaded compression metrics. Memory benchmarks reflect 41.63 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth and 24.61 GB/sec write bandwidth.

Without integrated local disks, the D4as_v5 balances baseline compute and memory density without incurring local NVMe overhead. Workload suitability centers on general-purpose enterprise tasks that do not require intense multi-threaded concurrency or local scratch arrays, such as lightweight application backends, mid-tier web serving, standard microservices, and development environments attached to managed block storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D4as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 3.525 GHz AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores. It features 16.0 GB of memory, delivering a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, accompanied by a 32 MB L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, depending instead on remote Premium Storage for disk operations. In benchmarks, the D4as_v5 exhibits strong single-core CPU execution alongside mid-range encryption and single-threaded decompression rates, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory write bandwidth remain constrained by its four-vCPU scale. This configuration is engineered for balanced enterprise workloads such as microservices, small-to-medium relational database instances, background batch processing, and standard web application hosting.
